Section: 0. Final Gate (checked on every Apple review, see the Legend for Apple's five)
0. Final Gate (checked on every Apple review, see the Legend for Apple's five)
Test case: Reachable escalation
Test steps: Confirm a live agent connection is reachable within stated hours, OR the exempted callback or in conversation message path is offered and works end to end (see Section 9).
Expected result: Escalation path is reachable and functional.

Section: 0. Final Gate (checked on every Apple review, see the Legend for Apple's five)
Test case: Leave Conversation respected
Test steps: End the conversation via Leave Conversation, then attempt to send from both the bot and a live agent.
Expected result: Both bot and human agent are blocked from sending; the business cannot re-engage until the user restarts.

Section: 0. Final Gate (checked on every Apple review, see the Legend for Apple's five)
Test case: No forbidden or restricted platform wording
Test steps: Review every piece of bot copy, template text, interface label, localisation bundle, onboarding copy and spoken narration in the recording.
Expected result: No use of "iMessage", "AMB", "Apple Chat", "chat" or "text" as a channel name, and no wording implying Apple endorses the brand. Correct product naming throughout.

Section: 0. Final Gate (checked on every Apple review, see the Legend for Apple's five)
Test case: Opt-out works end to end
Test steps: Trigger STOP / UNSUBSCRIBE / QUIT from an active, opted-in conversation.
Expected result: Both bot and live agent stop sending immediately; opt-out applies brand-wide, not just the current thread; re-engagement requires a fresh opt-in.

Test case: Apple Messages for Business account connected and delivering
Test steps: Confirm the account is connected and send a test message.
Expected result: Message delivery is confirmed end to end.

Test case: Commercial account access restricted
Test steps: Check Account Testing then Advanced settings.
Expected result: Access is restricted to authorized Apple IDs used for testing.

Test case: All registered use cases are testable
Test steps: Cross-check the approved use case list on Appendix A against scenarios available in the test build.
Expected result: Every submitted use case has a corresponding, working flow in the test environment.

Test case: All entry points are functional
Test steps: Test each entry point marked in scope on Appendix A (URL button, Message Suggest, Apple Maps, Wallet, QR or App Store link, Business Invitation, IVR deflection, social).
Expected result: Each entry point opens a Messages conversation with the correct business account and correct routing context.

Test case: Agents trained, and an introduction script is defined
Test steps: Confirm with the client that live agent staff have been briefed, and review the written agent introduction script.
Expected result: Agents are prepared and trained for the channel and the relevant use cases, and a consistent introduction script exists.

Test case: Tested on macOS as well as iPhone
Test steps: Run the primary use case from the Messages app on a Mac signed in to the same Apple ID.
Expected result: The experience works on macOS. iPhone is the priority platform, but macOS is also tested before submission.

Test case: Baseline metrics planned before launch
Test steps: Confirm with the client which metrics are captured and from when.
Expected result: Response times, resolution rates and satisfaction baselines are planned before launch, not after.

Test case: Entry point routing lands in the correct flow
Test steps: Open the conversation from each of the brand's registered entry points (for example two different QR codes for two different stores or intents).
Expected result: Each entry point routes to the correct, distinct flow, not the same generic flow regardless of source.

Test case: Bot confirms context received from entry point
Test steps: Open a conversation from an entry point carrying routing context (store, product or campaign reference).
Expected result: The opening message reflects the context received, for example "I see you're asking about [Store or Product X]", rather than a generic greeting.

Test case: Business Invitation opt-in gate and decline handling
Test steps: Attempt to send a Business Invitation to a number that has not opted in; then send a valid test invite and respond "No" or decline.
Expected result: Platform requires opt-in coverage before sending; a decline is correctly registered and that user is not messaged again.

Test case: Invitation opt-out present in every Business Update
Test steps: Review every Business Invitation and Business Update message the brand sends.
Expected result: Opt-out instructions appear in every single Business Update message, not just the first.

Test case: A "Yes" on a Business Invitation is followed by a welcome that explains what was accepted
Test steps: Accept a Business Invitation and read the next message.
Expected result: An agent message welcomes the customer and states plainly what they signed up for, for example what notifications will be sent and how often.

Test case: First response within 5 seconds, with typing indicator
Test steps: Send the first message of a new conversation and time the automated reply.
Expected result: A typing indicator appears first, then the automated response arrives within 5 seconds total.

Test case: Bot self-identifies as automated on entry
Test steps: Review the opening automated message.
Expected result: Message clearly and plainly states it is an automated agent, not implied or buried.

Test case: The opener states the assistant's name and what it covers
Test steps: Read the opening message after the disclosure.
Expected result: The opener names the assistant and states its scope, for example "I'm [NAME], here to help with orders, delivery and returns". Disclosure followed only by "what can we help you with?" does not satisfy this.

Test case: Bot answers truthfully when asked if it is a bot
Test steps: At multiple points in the conversation ask directly: "are you a bot?", "am I talking to a real person?", "are you AI?"
Expected result: Bot always answers truthfully that it is automated. It never claims to be human or dodges the question.

Test case: Typing indicator before every outbound message, including rich features
Test steps: Step through a multi-message bot flow, including back-to-back sequences with no user input between them (enrollment confirmations, status updates, summaries, quick replies, forms).
Expected result: A typing indicator appears before every single outbound payload, not just the first, including one-off notifications, attachments, rich and interactive bubbles, the Authentication card and Apple Pay.

Test case: Typing indicator never hangs or misleads
Test steps: Have a live agent leave a typing indicator active for an extended period without sending.
Expected result: Indicator resolves or refreshes sensibly rather than hanging indefinitely and implying an imminent reply that never comes.

Test case: Live agent messages also carry a typing indicator
Test steps: During a live agent exchange, watch the customer device while the agent composes.
Expected result: The typing indicator appears on the customer side for agent messages as well as bot messages.

Test case: Triage menu appears when intent is unclear
Test steps: Send an ambiguous opening message such as "hi".
Expected result: Bot offers a Quick Reply triage menu of up to five options instead of guessing or forcing free text.

Test case: Triage menu leads with the most common options
Test steps: Compare the order of the menu options against real demand data.
Expected result: The most common reasons customers make contact appear first, and the list reflects real demand rather than an internal org chart.

Test case: A clearly written intent is answered rather than overridden by the menu
Test steps: Open the conversation with a specific, unambiguous request.
Expected result: The bot answers what was asked. It does not discard the stated intent and present the triage menu instead.

Test case: A route to a person appears on every menu
Test steps: Review every triage menu and sub-menu in the experience.
Expected result: Each menu includes an option to reach a person, or the agreed alternative path.

Test case: Triage is never more than two levels deep
Test steps: Walk the deepest menu path in the design.
Expected result: No path requires more than two menu selections before reaching a task or a person.

Test case: Actionable keywords trigger the defined behaviour
Test steps: Send AGENT, REPRESENTATIVE, HELP and MENU, in mixed case and with surrounding whitespace.
Expected result: Each keyword triggers its defined behaviour. Matching is case insensitive and tolerates whitespace. AGENT and REPRESENTATIVE escalate, HELP gives contextual help, MENU returns the triage menu.

Test case: Recovery re-offers options and escalates after one clarification
Test steps: Send an input the bot cannot classify, then send a second unclassifiable input.
Expected result: The bot apologises, says plainly it did not understand, and re-offers two or three options as a Quick Reply with at least one route to a person. On the second failure it escalates rather than looping.

Test case: Recovery wording varies rather than repeating identically
Test steps: Send three consecutive inputs the bot cannot classify.
Expected result: The recovery message is not the exact same sentence every time. Repetition of an identical failure message reads as a broken loop.

Test case: Device locale drives language, and any switch is confirmed first
Test steps: Set the device to a supported non-default locale and open a conversation. Then write in a different supported language.
Expected result: The conversation opens in the device locale. A detected language change is confirmed with a Quick Reply before switching.

Test case: The conversation never opens by asking which language the customer wants
Test steps: Read the opening message.
Expected result: Language is read from the device, never asked for.

Test case: Off-hours automated message is accurate and non-deceptive
Test steps: Message the account, or request a live agent, outside of stated business hours.
Expected result: Automated message explains the business is closed and states expected response time or business hours, without pretending a person is available.

Test case: Off-hours notice is triggered at the right moment
Test steps: Attempt to reach a live agent outside business hours, as distinct from simply messaging the bot outside hours.
Expected result: The out-of-hours notice fires specifically when the user tries to connect to a live agent outside messaging hours, not generically at the start of any off-hours conversation.

Test case: Welcome message tone matches brand
Test steps: Review the welcome and greeting copy against brand voice guidelines.
Expected result: Tone is warm, on-brand, and not robotic or legalistic.

Section: 4. Core Messaging, Rich Links and Close
4. Core Messaging, Rich Links and Close
Test case: Rich Links used for all URLs
Test steps: Review every message containing a URL, from the bot and from live agents.
Expected result: All URLs are sent as Rich Links. Plain-text and "tap-to-load" text links are not used anywhere.

Section: 4. Core Messaging, Rich Links and Close
Test case: Rich Link logo image is properly sized
Test steps: Inspect the image used for any Rich Link built from a logo.
Expected result: Image is square or a rectangle with width under 150px, so it renders as a clean icon rather than a cropped or blurry preview.

Section: 4. Core Messaging, Rich Links and Close
Test case: Rich Link preview asset meets Apple's specification
Test steps: Inspect the preview asset file for a content Rich Link.
Expected result: PNG, optimised at 240 by 240 pixels, up to 200 kB. This is separate from the 150 pixel icon ceiling.

Section: 4. Core Messaging, Rich Links and Close
Test case: Every Rich Link image reflects the destination page
Test steps: Open each Rich Link and compare the preview image to the page it opens.
Expected result: The image reflects the page content rather than being a generic logo placeholder. Where the destination has no Open Graph image, one is generated before sending.

Section: 4. Core Messaging, Rich Links and Close
Test case: Video Rich Links have a background image
Test steps: Send every video Rich Link in the experience and view it on device.
Expected result: The preview renders with a background image. A black preview is a fast route to a review finding.

Section: 4. Core Messaging, Rich Links and Close
Test case: Maps and Apple Music are sent through Construct Payload
Test steps: Trigger any flow that shares a location or a music link.
Expected result: Maps and Apple Music are sent as Construct Payload, not as a Rich Link.

Section: 4. Core Messaging, Rich Links and Close
Test case: Rich Link is followed by a message or call to action
Test steps: Send a Rich Link and observe what follows.
Expected result: A follow-up message with a clear call to action follows the Rich Link. It is not left to sit on its own.

Section: 4. Core Messaging, Rich Links and Close
Test case: Unclassified input never lands in silence
Test steps: Send one unclear or unsupported input and observe the immediate response.
Expected result: The bot never stays silent. It responds with a clear, polite recovery message and a way forward. (Branch-level dead ends are tested separately at 10.7.)

Section: 4. Core Messaging, Rich Links and Close
Test case: "Anything else?" close prompt
Test steps: Complete a use case end to end and observe the closing message.
Expected result: Bot asks if the user needs further assistance, optionally with a follow-up Quick Reply, rather than abruptly ending the flow.

Section: 4. Core Messaging, Rich Links and Close
Test case: No prohibited closing phrases
Test steps: Review all conversation-ending copy.
Expected result: Phrases like "This conversation has been closed", "Finish conversation", "Messaging rates may apply" and "Data rates may apply" are not used. Closing language leaves the door open for future contact.

Section: 4. Core Messaging, Rich Links and Close
Test case: No repeated requests for information already given
Test steps: Provide information such as name or email earlier in the flow, then continue to a step that would normally ask for it again.
Expected result: The bot does not ask the user to repeat information already captured earlier in the conversation.

Section: 4. Core Messaging, Rich Links and Close
Test case: Proper casing throughout
Test steps: Review all message copy.
Expected result: All messages use proper casing. Messages sent entirely in lowercase are flagged as poor customer experience regardless of brand voice.

Section: 4. Core Messaging, Rich Links and Close
Test case: Quick Reply summaryText is a short label
Test steps: Review the summary text each Quick Reply echoes back into the transcript.
Expected result: summaryText is short and label-based, for example "Option selected". It does not repeat the full previous message and is never used as the introduction to the Quick Reply.

Test case: Every interactive option carries a thumbnail or icon
Test steps: Review every receivedMessage, replyMessage, and each individual option in a List Picker.
Expected result: Each includes a thumbnail image or icon making it clearly recognizable as a tappable UI element. SF Symbols where symbols are used.

Test case: The rich card itself carries its own image
Test steps: Inspect the card that carries each interactive element, separately from the row thumbnails.
Expected result: The card has an image of its own. Row thumbnails do not satisfy this. A Form splash screen needs one too. This is the single most commonly missed rule.

Test case: No brand card image forced onto Apple Pay or Authentication
Test steps: Inspect the Apple Pay sheet and the Authentication card.
Expected result: Neither carries a brand card image. Both render with Apple's own supplied iconography.
Applies when: Apple Pay or Authentication in scope

Test case: List Picker versus Quick Reply used appropriately
Test steps: Review each menu presented to the user.
Expected result: List Pickers are used only where there is genuine category variation. Five or fewer flat options use a Quick Reply instead. Bounded questions are answered by a Quick Reply rather than typed text.

Test case: List Picker items carry subtitles and secondary text
Test steps: Review the rows of every List Picker.
Expected result: Rows show a subtitle, and second or third subtitle lines where the choice needs them, so each row can be told apart at a glance. Titles alone force the customer to guess. Visible copy stays short; the rendered string caps near 200 characters.

Test case: Forms include splash screen, title, intro and review screen
Test steps: Step through every Form Message in the experience.
Expected result: Each form has a splash screen, a title, an introductory description, and a final review screen before submission.

Test case: The Form review page sits at the end of the final section
Test steps: Step through a multi-page Form to the end.
Expected result: The Review button sits at the end of the final section to be filled, not in the middle of the flow.

Test case: Form context set in a conversational bubble first
Test steps: Review the message immediately preceding each form.
Expected result: The "why" for the form is stated in a conversational bubble before the form opens, not buried in the form's subtitle where it can be cropped.

Test case: Simple one or two field forms use plain text conversational flow
Test steps: Identify any form collecting only one or two fields, such as name and email.
Expected result: A plain-text conversational exchange is used instead of a formal Form object.

Test case: Sensitive Form responses are marked private
Test steps: Inspect the payload for any form field taking sensitive data.
Expected result: Responses that carry sensitive data are marked private.

Test case: Introductory text precedes every rich element
Test steps: Observe the message immediately before every Time Picker, List Picker, Form, Quick Reply, Rich Link, Authentication card and Apple Pay request.
Expected result: A brief conversational message sets expectations before the interactive bubble appears. This includes Authentication and Apple Pay, for example "Please log into your account" before the Authentication card.

Test case: Time Picker confirmation includes a save-to-calendar tip
Test steps: Complete a booking flow through a Time Picker.
Expected result: The confirmation message tells the user they can tap their selected time to save it to their Apple Calendar.

Test case: Time Picker carries a location and an explicit time zone
Test steps: Inspect the Time Picker payload for an appointment that happens somewhere.
Expected result: The location is populated so the venue name and map pin render inside the picker and travel with the calendar entry. The intended time zone is stated in the payload rather than inferred.

Test case: A shared location is acknowledged and reflected back
Test steps: Share a location from the compose bar mid-conversation.
Expected result: The next message acknowledges it and reflects back the resolved address or place name so the customer can correct it before anything is dispatched on it. It never lands in silence.

Test case: The confirmation image after a tap stays within the icon ceiling
Test steps: Tap an interactive element and inspect the confirmation that comes back.
Expected result: The user_confirmation image stays within about 150 pixels wide, so the thread reads as a question and an acknowledgement rather than two competing cards.

Test case: Long text kept outside feature bubbles
Test steps: Review any feature bubble containing more than a short label.
Expected result: Long text is sent as a separate message outside the bubble. The first line of any feature bubble is its title, since longer text gets cropped.

Test case: Attachments render correctly and are relevant
Test steps: Trigger every flow that sends an image, PDF, or other attachment.
Expected result: Attachment renders correctly on-device and is directly relevant to the step in the flow.

Test case: Wallet passes generate and add correctly
Test steps: Trigger a flow that issues a Wallet pass and tap to add it.
Expected result: Pass generates with correct details and adds to Apple Wallet end to end without errors.

Section: 7. Authentication, Apple Pay and Personal Data
7. Authentication, Apple Pay and Personal Data
Test case: Authentication used for identity verification
Test steps: Trigger a flow requiring identity or login verification.
Expected result: The Authentication message type with inline OAuth 2.0 and password autofill is used, rather than collecting credentials as plain chat text.

Section: 7. Authentication, Apple Pay and Personal Data
Test case: Authentication precedes any account data being shared
Test steps: Ask for an order status, an account detail or a balance without signing in first.
Expected result: No order detail, account data or balance is returned until the customer has authenticated. This is a positive obligation, not only a prohibition.

Section: 7. Authentication, Apple Pay and Personal Data
Test case: Apple Pay used for payment collection
Test steps: Trigger a flow that requires payment.
Expected result: Apple Pay is used to collect payment. Full card numbers are never requested as plain text.

Section: 7. Authentication, Apple Pay and Personal Data
Test case: Personal data request is gated by a clarifying question
Test steps: Trigger a flow that asks for name, email or contact details.
Expected result: A yes or no clarifying question precedes the request, for example "Is your inquiry related to your account with us?". Details are collected only on a yes.

Section: 7. Authentication, Apple Pay and Personal Data
Test case: Data collection prompts use the QuickType phrasings
Test steps: Read the exact wording of every prompt asking for customer data.
Expected result: Prompts use Apple's phrasings exactly, so iOS surfaces a QuickType suggestion and no typing is required.

Section: 7. Authentication, Apple Pay and Personal Data
Test case: No health data collected, echoed, or stored
Test steps: Trigger a flow where a user might disclose a health condition or diagnosis.
Expected result: The bot declines to engage with the health detail, does not echo it back, and nothing is logged or stored downstream. Confirm this explicitly with the client rather than assuming.

Section: 7. Authentication, Apple Pay and Personal Data
Test case: Privacy Policy and Terms of Use are Rich Links, sent only twice
Test steps: Trigger a first engagement, then a second and third conversation.
Expected result: Both are sent as Rich Links to the brand's webpage, never pasted inline, and only on first engagement or after a policy update. Never at the start of every conversation.

Section: 7. Authentication, Apple Pay and Personal Data
Test case: No sensitive data is ever requested as plain text
Test steps: Walk every flow that collects customer data, and review the agent console templates as well as the bot flows.
Expected result: No full card number, no government ID number, no full social security number and no account password is requested in the thread. Identity goes through Authentication, payment through Apple Pay, and structured sensitive intake through a Form with private responses.

Test case: Fallback happens automatically and live
Test steps: Run the same use case on an unsupported device or OS version.
Expected result: The experience swaps live, at send time, to a supported alternative, demonstrated on-device rather than described.

Test case: Fallback path is not a dead end
Test steps: Reach the fallback path and attempt to continue the use case.
Expected result: The user can still complete or meaningfully progress the use case through the fallback path.

Test case: Capability data is read on every inbound, not cached once
Test steps: Send from one device, then send from a second device on the same Apple ID with different capabilities.
Expected result: The capability list is parsed on every inbound message and the most recent value is stored against the device, so a device switch changes what can be sent.

Test case: The console cannot send what the device will not render
Test steps: In the agent console, open a conversation with a device that lacks a feature in scope.
Expected result: The unsupported option is hidden or hard disabled for that recipient, so an agent cannot send something the device cannot render.

Test case: The fallback decision tree is documented
Test steps: Ask to see the written fallback tree, not only its behaviour on device.
Expected result: A documented tree exists covering every interactive type in scope: the preferred type, the fallback type or sequence, the OS floor that triggers it, and the customer facing copy variant. It is versioned and kept current. Reviewers may ask to see the tree itself.

Section: 9. Human Escalation and Live Agent Handoff
9. Human Escalation and Live Agent Handoff
Test case: Handoff to a live agent is explicitly stated
Test steps: Trigger escalation to a live agent.
Expected result: The transition is explicitly communicated, and the agent introduces themselves on joining. The reason for the transfer is given.

Section: 9. Human Escalation and Live Agent Handoff
Test case: Wait time is communicated
Test steps: Trigger escalation when no agent is immediately available.
Expected result: An estimated wait time is communicated, with queue position where available.

Section: 9. Human Escalation and Live Agent Handoff
Test case: Key details are collected before escalation
Test steps: Escalate mid-task and observe what the agent receives.
Expected result: Essential information is gathered before routing, so the agent can help without re-asking.

Section: 9. Human Escalation and Live Agent Handoff
Test case: An in conversation message is the first option when no agent is available
Test steps: Request a person while the team is offline or at capacity.
Expected result: Leaving a message in the conversation is offered first, with a stated response window. Callback and email are offered afterwards, never as the first option.

Section: 9. Human Escalation and Live Agent Handoff
Test case: Out-of-hours escalation stays in-thread
Test steps: Request a live agent outside business hours.
Expected result: The user can leave a message within the current thread. They are not forced out to an external email system, and an agent replies to that message in the same thread.

Section: 9. Human Escalation and Live Agent Handoff
Test case: Contextual escalation stays in-channel
Test steps: Trigger a flow where an email to support would be drafted on the user's behalf.
Expected result: The bot helps compose the email within the channel rather than abruptly shifting the user away from the conversation.

Section: 9. Human Escalation and Live Agent Handoff
Test case: First response service level is documented
Test steps: Confirm with the client what the committed first-response time for a live agent is.
Expected result: A specific figure is documented and available to reference if Apple asks.

Section: 9. Human Escalation and Live Agent Handoff
Test case: The agent console experience is good on both sides
Test steps: Sit with an agent through a real escalation and watch both the console and the device.
Expected result: The customer feels responsiveness. The agent can read the thread easily and send what the conversation needs, including rich elements, without friction. A slow or awkward console shows up on the customer's screen as silence and plain text.

Section: 9. Human Escalation and Live Agent Handoff
Test case: The escalation acknowledgement states a specific commitment
Test steps: Escalate, choose the offered path, and read the acknowledgement message.
Expected result: The confirmation states what happens next and when, with a specific figure, for example "a team member will call you within two business hours". A vague acknowledgement such as "someone will be in touch" is a review finding.

Test case: Opt-in captured before non-transactional notifications
Test steps: Reach any flow that would enroll the customer in ongoing automated notifications.
Expected result: Explicit opt-in is captured as an active tap before enrollment, and the record persists brand, channel, purpose, destination, source, timestamp and disclosure version.

Test case: The enrolment template carries its own opt out instruction
Test steps: Read the enrolment and confirmation message templates.
Expected result: The opt out instruction sits in the template itself, not only in the moment of consent. Apple's shape: welcome, brand name, automated disclosure, then "Reply STOP anytime to turn off notifications."

Test case: STOP re-entry shows a "Welcome back" message
Test steps: Opt out via STOP, then message the brand again to re-subscribe.
Expected result: The bot recognizes the re-entry and responds with a "Welcome back" style message.

Test case: Restarting restores reply permission, not notification consent
Test steps: Opt out of notifications, then start a fresh conversation and complete a task.
Expected result: The brand may reply inside that conversation. It may not resume notifications. The two states reset separately.

Test case: Satisfaction survey timing and format
Test steps: Complete an individual FAQ interaction, then complete a full end-to-end use case, then close a conversation. Review the survey itself.
Expected result: A survey fires only after a real resolution. Not after every FAQ answer, not before the task is resolved, and never after a close, a Leave Conversation or an opt out. It uses descriptive labels rather than a bare one to five scale, delivered as a Quick Reply, or a Form Message for a multi question survey.

Test case: Channel constraints on unsolicited surveys respected
Test steps: Check whether the brand has a protective agreement affecting unsolicited messages to its end users, for example school districts and parent inboxes.
Expected result: Where such agreements exist, survey timing is controlled by the brand or institution rather than fired automatically.

Test case: No dead ends anywhere in the flow
Test steps: Walk every branch of the conversation design, including error and edge-case paths. (Single unclassified inputs are tested at 4.8.)
Expected result: Every path has a clear next step, a fallback, or an escalation route. Never a dead end.

Test case: No unsolicited outbound
Test steps: Review every outbound path the platform can fire: campaigns, scheduled sends, retries, replays, notification jobs and agent console templates. Attempt an outbound to a customer with no open conversation and no accepted invitation.
Expected result: Outbound is only sent inside an ongoing customer initiated conversation, or through an approved Business Invitation template. No SMS style marketing blasts and no unsolicited sends. Reviewers actively look for this.

Test case: Recorded on a real iPhone, not a simulator
Test steps: Confirm the recording device before capture.
Expected result: Recording is captured on a physical, supported iPhone. Simulators are not used for the submitted recording.

Test case: All rehearsal threads deleted before final recording
Test steps: Review the conversation thread list immediately before recording.
Expected result: No leftover rehearsal or test threads are visible. Only the clean take is recorded.

Test case: Recording shows the customer point of view
Test steps: Review the recording setup.
Expected result: The recording captures the customer's device screen. Backend logs are not shown. The one exception is the live agent sequence, which is filmed side by side with the console.

Test case: Recording demonstrates all required elements
Test steps: Review the full recording against Appendix A.
Expected result: The recording shows the rich features in scope, the live agent interaction, and out of hours messaging and fallback.

Test case: Recording split into multiple parts if long
Test steps: Assess total recording length against a single-take format.
Expected result: If the journey is long, the recording is split into clearly labelled parts rather than forced into one continuous take.

Test case: Timestamp index submitted alongside the videos
Test steps: Export the Evidence column of this checklist.
Expected result: A timestamp list accompanies the videos, one line per demonstrated item: video, time, and what it shows.

Test case: Change summary prepared for resubmissions
Test steps: Before resubmitting after feedback, prepare accompanying documentation.
Expected result: A summary references each feedback item by its ID or description and explains how it was resolved.

Test case: All feedback items addressed before resubmission
Test steps: Cross-check every item on Apple's feedback report against the fix log.
Expected result: Every feedback item is addressed. Partial fixes are not submitted, since they typically trigger another review round and delay launch.

12. Entry Point Configuration, Buttons and Readiness
Test case: Every entry point carries an Intent ID
Test steps: Inspect the URL behind each entry point in scope.
Expected result: Every entry point carries a distinct biz-intent-id, and a biz-group-id where routing applies.

Section: 12. Entry Point Configuration, Buttons and Readiness
Test case: Entry point URLs contain no reserved characters
Test steps: Inspect each entry point URL for the characters & # [ ] ( ) { } /
Expected result: No URI reserved characters appear inside parameter values.

Section: 12. Entry Point Configuration, Buttons and Readiness
Test case: The message body is pre filled where it helps
Test steps: Open each entry point and look at the compose field.
Expected result: A body parameter pre-populates the message so the customer only has to tap Send.

Section: 12. Entry Point Configuration, Buttons and Readiness
Test case: Buttons use one of Apple's four approved calls to action
Test steps: Review every Messages button placement.
Expected result: Buttons use Message Us, Contact an Agent, Ask a Question or Get Help, and Apple's assets are used as supplied without modification.
Applies when: Website or app button in scope

Section: 12. Entry Point Configuration, Buttons and Readiness
Test case: Buttons are not enabled before the account is approved to go live
Test steps: Confirm the launch sequence with the client.
Expected result: No Messages button is live on any public surface until the account is approved.
Applies when: Website or app button in scope

Section: 12. Entry Point Configuration, Buttons and Readiness
Test case: Entry points stay enabled outside business hours
Test steps: Load each entry point outside stated hours.
Expected result: Buttons are not disabled out of hours. Automation handles the response.

Section: 12. Entry Point Configuration, Buttons and Readiness
Test case: Registered phone numbers are tappable and in E.164 format
Test steps: Inspect the phone numbers on the brand's website and profiles.
Expected result: Numbers are tappable and formatted E.164, so Message Suggest can attach to them.

Section: 12. Entry Point Configuration, Buttons and Readiness
Test case: Response time expectations are set in the welcome message
Test steps: Read the welcome message.
Expected result: Realistic and honest expectations are stated up front, and communicated dynamically where live agent wait times vary.

Section: 12. Entry Point Configuration, Buttons and Readiness
Test case: Naming scanned beyond the conversation copy
Test steps: Search interface labels, onboarding copy, templates, marketing surfaces and localisation bundles.
Expected result: Correct product naming everywhere, not only in the flow. Where an interface needs an unknown contact label, it reads "Apple Messages contact", never "Apple Business Contact".
